hook: SCP-3426 is a Keter entry about a phenomenon that has wiped out every advanced alien civilization the Foundation has managed to find. The early sections read like a checklist, and it pays to hold that checklist up against present-day Earth before moving on to the planets. The recovered documents near the end, including an emergency broadcast and a handwritten note, are bleak and touch on suicide and people dissolving out of existence. The page stops at a Level 4 clearance prompt, and the exploration log it points to is a separate page not covered here.
whyItMatters: The horror lives in a list of conditions: the article never shows the cause, only the shared traits of the worlds it erased, and leaves the reader to notice what those traits imply. Its containment procedures are unusual because they ask the Foundation to slow down physics and energy research rather than lock anything in a cell. The planet entries also work as compact sketches of very different alien societies, each ending in its own kind of collapse.
thingsToNotice: The sixth condition, an organization devoted to cataloguing and containing anomalies, is the twist hiding in plain sight, and post-3426-13 had a Foundation counterpart whose sites have become spheres of total darkness. Every planet breaks differently: water locked into one rigid solid, chemistry made impossible, time slowing unevenly until it stops, whole regions displaced from the surface. The documents grow more personal as they go, from a researcher frightened by the equation he is about to finish, to a looping broadcast teaching people how to fade quietly, to a council admitting it learned too much, to a note whose words fall apart as its writer forgets them. The remark that post-3426-10's people spoke something close to Hittite is left under review, one of several threads the article never resolves.
